title: [feature] Home in affectUI: Home renders from one HomeView(props: HomeData) with no fetch, on the kit's components (kpi-chart per north star, empty state, skeletons), every kept text word for word, in both themes; checked by a server-side render
prompt:
Spawn, mission 4, objective 120 [feature]: Home in affectUI. The Home page is rebuilt on the kit's components, with the same data, wording, behaviour and routes. Its markup comes from one component that takes its data as props, so a script can render it and read what a user sees. It is the first page of the affectUI series (the owner via lead-mac, 11-13 14:02 and 15:00), after 119 (affectUI's tokens set from Spawn's theme roles, web/src/styles/aui.css). Size: one page per objective, the owner's order; size exception granted by the lead. The restyle of every block on the kit's frame belongs here, with a soft ceiling of about 600 changed lines (past that, tell the lead).

The kit and its source (the owner, 11-13 15:00). The kit's components are copied byte for byte into web/src/components/ui/ by the lead's owner push, with a sha256 list (119's check). This objective edits none of them. The source stays inside the private repository: it is not published anywhere outside it, and no part of it is quoted in a sync note, a review, a contract or a notice.

The seam (the lead's decision). Home's markup is rendered by a component that takes its data as props: web/src/components/home/HomeView.tsx exports `HomeView(props: HomeData)` and the type `HomeData`. HomeView renders from its props only: no fetch, no poll, and no effect needed for its first paint. The fetching stays where it is today (App's polls, and FleetView's polls for the alerts window, the interventions and the core lines), and passes the data down. `HomeData` is exactly these fields, each made by Spawn's existing pure modules and types (web/src/home.ts, interventions.ts, coreLines.ts), which this objective does not change:
- now: number (ms; the time the models were made for);
- needs: NeedItem[];
- missions: MissionsToday;
- agents: AgentsNow;
- notes: NotesShown; allNotes: NoteRow[];
- digest: Digest; back: number | null (when the reader came back, useAway);
- interventions: { day: FigureState; week: FigureState } (figureState of /api/interventions for 24h and 7d);
- coreLines: { answer: CoreLinesAnswer | null; error: string | null } (/api/core-lines; both null while loading);
- talk: ReactNode (the box that types to the supervisor);
- onOpenAgent: (session: string) => void; onShowMissions: () => void.
Every module HomeView imports must load without a browser beyond a bare window (an address, empty storage, a fetch that fails): nothing reads the DOM at import time.

What Home uses (rev-b's fit of the kit to Home's data, the lead's decision). Kit files are imported through Spawn's own door in web/src/components/aui/, which imports each by its full path ("../ui/kpi-chart"), never "../ui" alone (that is Spawn's own components/ui.tsx):
- card, badge, button, tooltip, skeleton and empty-state: the frame of every block (each card on the kit's card, its badges, buttons and tooltips the kit's). "Nothing needs you." is the kit's empty state, and a block still loading shows the kit's skeleton.
- kpi-chart: each core line's north star. Its title is the north star's name and its value is coreLinesView's value text exactly. Its series is the north star's trend points (/api/core-lines gives them), its footer the range text, and its plot carries the kit's own label "<name> chart …". No delta: kpi-chart colours a positive change green, which is wrong where lower is better. Its `format` words a number in the north star's unit (coreLines.ts's unitWords), so the axis and the tooltip carry the unit as the value does (rev-g's N1).
- segmented-control stays as it is (the theme switch is in the Sidebar, which this objective does not change).
- Not used, because they do not fit Home's data or would add behaviour: decision-inbox, agent-inbox, running-now, project-card, chat-composer, away-summary, agent-recap, compact-breakdown, usage-meter, progress-tracker, and kpi-chart for the interventions (their API gives two figures and a list, no series). Those blocks keep Spawn's own markup.

Required behaviour. Everything Home shows and does today stays:
- Needs you: the summary; each item's title, since, more/less detail, the command to copy and its Copy button, Resume, Open, and the line "Should not have been raised?" with its command, word for word. "Nothing needs you." when empty.
- Missions (today): each row, its in-flight tasks, the last sent-back line, "Nothing open: …", "<n> closed", and the no-work text.
- Working now and the idle names, each opening its agent.
- From the supervisor: the notes, the "N more · N earlier" or "settled" toggle, the earlier and settled marks, and the input box as it is (InputBox: Enter sends, Shift+Enter a new line, the stopped state).
- Today / Since you were away, folded to its counts, then its bands.
- Human interventions: the two figures (24 h and 7 d), their counts and retries, "Which interventions", and the failed-read lines.
- Core lines: the notice, the pending lines, each north star and its range and trend, the restore-drill rows, and each guardrail's value, range, tone and trend. Every number, range and wording ("not collected yet", "measuring since", "never passed", "no drill") stays exactly as the pure modules produce it.
- Every route, link and poll stays. No API, model or pure module changes (web/src/*.ts stay as they are, and so does every existing web test).
- Readability: "Needs you" and the Core lines card are at least as readable as today. The page fits 1400 px and a phone width (375 px). It holds in dark and light. Reduced motion is honoured: the kit's own rules apply, and nothing new moves without them.
- Icons (the lead's decision): Home keeps lucide-react in this objective and imports nothing from @hugeicons/core-free-icons. The kit's badge and empty-state take icon data as a prop; a constant written in Spawn's code is fine. For any later import of the package, rev-g's conditions hold: (C1) icons only as constants imported at build time, never icon data from an API or from storage; (C2) deep imports (`@hugeicons/core-free-icons/<Name>`), never `import *`, the barrel or ./loader.
- Escape (rev-g's note): an open tooltip or popover takes Escape first. Where one sits near Spawn's own Escape handlers (the slide-over in web/src/components/ui.tsx, Sidebar, MissionTimeline, TraceView, the terminal key map), the first Escape closes it and a second reaches Spawn's handler. kpi-chart calls preventDefault on Escape inside its own plot even with nothing highlighted. Home has no dialog around it, so nothing is lost today. A later page that puts one inside a dialog must handle it.

What the fleet can show without a browser. There is no DOM test runner in web/, and adding one is the owner's to approve. react-dom/server comes with react-dom: no new dependency, and check-web's reviewed set is unchanged. So the scenario renders HomeView on the server and reads its HTML. Layout, colour and motion are read by lead-mac's screenshots.

Files (expected; no other open objective touches them):
- web/src/components/home/HomeView.tsx (new);
- web/src/components/home/Home.tsx;
- web/src/components/home/CoreLines.tsx;
- web/src/components/fleet/Interventions.tsx;
- web/src/components/fleet/FleetView.tsx (Home's data and layout only);
- Spawn's own door and compositions under web/src/components/aui/.
The throwaway (the seam, kpi-chart for the north stars, the kit's empty state and skeletons, no restyle beyond that) is +152 −54. Restyling every block on the kit's frame belongs in this objective (the size exception above), up to about 600 changed lines.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/120.sh. Black box over the tree under test (the working directory), with made-up data:
(1) `npm run build` (tsc, then vite) passes into a directory of the scenario's own, and every web test passes (`node --test`).
(2) A server-side render of HomeView: `vite build --ssr` of an entry the scenario writes, run under node with a bare window. It renders a "full" data set (two Needs-you items, missions with work in flight, a send-back, a quiet mission and closed ones, agents working and idle, a supervisor note, both intervention windows, core lines with a north star in range and its 7-day trend, a north star "measuring since", a guardrail "not collected yet", drills "never passed" and "no drill") and an "empty" one (no Needs-you item, no mission work, interventions that failed to read, core lines loading). The rendered text holds every kept text word for word, as the pure modules make it.
(3) Each north star is drawn by the kit's KPI chart: an element labelled "<north star name> chart" per north star.
(4) No rendered text or attribute says "undefined", "NaN" or "[object Object]".
(5) Rendered under data-theme="dark" and "light": every --aui-* name the rendered markup reads is declared by Spawn's styles for that theme and resolves to a value through them (119's tokens).
On the base (3e08fb12 with 119's throwaway), 120.sh exits 1: "(2) the server-side render of HomeView does not build: … Could not resolve '../src/components/home/HomeView' in ssr/entry.tsx". 119.sh keeps passing.

Verified by: the gate runs 120.sh (and 119.sh) on the candidate. After the landing, lead-mac takes the after half of the screenshot pair, at 1400 px and at a phone width, in light and dark, beside the before (sync/home-before-affectui-2026-11-13.png). lead-mac reads it for the same content, a drawn north-star line in both themes (rev-g's N2), and at least the same readability of "Needs you" and Core lines, and posts it in sync.
